title: Runtime failure heatmap and mitigation inventory
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary:
This page inventories observed runtime failure modes across the inference serving stack, visualizes a simple heatmap (frequency vs. business impact), and prescribes detection signals, immediate mitigations, short-term remediation, and owners for each failure mode. The intention is to give on-call and reliability engineers a single reference to triage and reduce mean-time-to-recovery (MTTR) and to feed engineering priorities for long-term fixes.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: GPU-hosted inference runtime, kernel scheduling layer, KV cache, model swap logic, request routing, and edge cases at the gRPC/HTTP boundary. Does NOT cover CI/CD build failures or infra account provisioning.
- Audience: on-call SREs, runtime engineers, platform product owners, incident commanders.

How to use this page:
1) Use the heatmap & failure list to identify priority failure modes for the next reliability sprint.
2) Follow the "On-call quick playbook" for fast triage during incidents.
3) Open a JIRA ticket with the reference ID from the row when scheduling long-term remediation.

Heatmap overview (explanation):
- X axis: observed frequency (Rare / Occasional / Frequent).
- Y axis: business impact (Low / Medium / High) where High indicates customer-visible SLO breach or revenue impact.
- Cells marked H = high priority, M = medium, L = low.

Heatmap summary table:
| Failure mode | Frequency | Business impact | Priority |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kernel hang during large-batch attention kernels | Occasional | High | H |
| GPU OOM during long-context requests | Frequent | Medium | H |
| KV cache checksum mismatch / corruption | Rare | High | M |
| Model-swap oscillation under burst | Occasional | Medium | M |
| gRPC connection churn (KEEPALIVE timeout) | Frequent | Medium | H |
| Priority inversion causing high-p99 latency | Occasional | Medium | M |
| NVLink degradation across node pairs | Rare | High | M |
| Cold-start high-latency (backend warmup) | Frequent | Low | L |
| Telemetry sampling gap / delayed traces | Occasional | Low | L |

Failure catalog (detailed rows):
--
1) Kernel hang during large-batch attention kernels
- Symptoms / detection signals:
  - Spikes in per-kernel latency: GPU kernel 95th/99th > 5x baseline for attention_* kernels.
  - Work unit stuck in runtime dispatcher for > 10s (trace span not closed).
  - Node-level hostwatcher logs: "kernel launch timed out" messages.
  - Prometheus metric: runtime_kernel_active_seconds{kernel=\"attention\"} shows unbounded growth.
- Immediate on-call mitigation (quick):
  1. Identify affected host: check grafana "kernel latency by node" panel.
  2. Move traffic off host with /svc/orchestrator/drain (use orchestration job: curl -XPOST $ORCH/drain?node=<id>).
  3. If drain fails, escalate to infra to detach GPU from scheduler.
- Short-term remediation (0–72h):
  - Disable the specific kernel implementation on canary pools via feature flag: runtime.feature_flags.disable_attention_fastpath=true for the canary group.
  - Run the focused microbenchmark job (tag: attention-regress) to validate fallback performance.
- Long-term remediation (>72h):
  - Root-cause: race in kernel semaphore recycle path. Owner: runtime/kernel team.
  - Deliverable: new kernel handshake protocol and integration test (stress x1000) + canary rollout plan.
- SLO implications: p99 latency SLO for text.generate routes may be violated.
- Runbook links: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/gpu-kernel-latency-investigation-playbook-2024

2) GPU OOM during long-context requests
- Symptoms / detection signals:
  - OOM events logged by NVIDIA driver: "Out of memory" with stack trace referencing allocator.
  - Sudden increase in pod restarts with reason: OOMKilled.
  - Prom metric: node_gpu_memory_free_bytes dropping below 10% for > 30s.
- Immediate mitigation:
  1. Re-route long-context traffic to model-quantized variants via routing override: POST /internal/routing/override {"model": "gpt-large-q4", "route": "low-memory-pool"}.
  2. If possible, apply binary eviction on the node: kubectl scale deployment runtime-worker-<node> --replicas=0; then scale back after recover.
- Short-term remediation:
  - Add conservative per-session KV cache reservation for long-context models.
  - Lower max_sequence_length for public hosted routes for affected models.
- Long-term remediation:
  - Implement dynamic memory accounting at runtime to preflight allocations (owner: memory/allocator squad).
  - Add CI GPU OOM blast test to prevent regressions.
- SLO implications: availability and throughput SLOs of Dedicated customers may be affected.

3) KV cache checksum mismatch / corruption
- Symptoms:
  - Decodes start failing with token mismatch errors; session-level cache misses unusually high.
  - CRC mismatch logs: kvcache.[shard].checksum != expected in node logs.
- Immediate mitigation:
  1. Trigger per-shard cache validation job: /internal/kvcache/validate?shard=<id>.
  2. If corruption confirmed, invalidate shard: POST /internal/kvcache/invalidate?shard=<id>.
- Short-term remediation:
  - Add guardrail to pipeline to detect and auto-invalidate suspect shards at first sign of CRC failure.
- Long-term remediation:
  - Replace in-memory checksum with signed epoched checksums persisted to durable metadata store.
- Owner: kvcache team.

4) Model-swap oscillation under burst
- Symptoms:
  - Rapid back-and-forth model assignment logs: "swap to variant-A", then "swap to variant-B" for same session id within seconds.
  - Request latencies increase and error rates rise due to repeated reloads.
- Immediate mitigation:
  - Enable cooldown window via runtime flag for problematic deployments: routing.cooldown_seconds=60.
- Short-term remediation:
  - Adjust the swap decision thresholds; prefer sticky assignment for sessions < 30s.
- Long-term remediation:
  - Rework swap policy to incorporate tokenized cost and observed warmup penalty.
- Owner: routing/decisioning team.

5) gRPC connection churn (KEEPALIVE timeout)
- Symptoms:
  - Surge of gRPC CONNECT errors with code 14 in logs.
  - High number of new connection events and ephemeral connections; average connection lifetime < 2s.
  - Service-level metrics: requests_per_connection falls dramatically.
- Immediate mitigation:
  1. Increase keepalive timeout on load balancer for the affected pool: set envoy.cluster.connect_timeout to 15s.
  2. Apply temporary retry policy to smooth transient failures: retry_policy.per_route.max_retries=2.
- Short-term remediation:
  - Tune client keepalive and server read timeout alignment.
- Long-term remediation:
  - Add connection pooling proxy layer for unstable edge networks and harden backpressure logic.
- Owner: networking team.

6) Priority inversion causing high-p99 latency
- Symptoms:
  - Low-priority batches blocking high-priority short requests due to long-running kernel occupancy.
  - Scheduler queue depth for high-priority class spikes while low-priority queue drains slowly.
- Immediate mitigation:
  - Enable preemptive slice for the affected host: runtime.scheduler.preemptive_slices=true.
- Short-term remediation:
  - Implement admission control that rejects large batch jobs when high-priority queue > threshold (e.g., 50).
- Long-term remediation:
  - Improve scheduler credit accounting and introduce kernel-level preemption signals.
- Owner: scheduler team.

7) NVLink degradation across node pairs
- Symptoms:
  - Inter-GPU bandwidth drop; cross-node allreduce times increase; model shardization latency rises.
  - Kernel-level errors referencing nvlink_qpair timeouts.
- Immediate mitigation:
  - Evacuate cross-node sharded workloads to same-node placement using scheduler hint: place_same_node=true.
- Short-term remediation:
  - Replace or re-seat NVLink cables and run vendor diagnostics.
- Long-term remediation:
  - Add NVLink health telemetry and automatic reroute rules in topology-aware scheduler.
- Owner: GPU-Fleet team.

8) Cold-start high-latency (backend warmup)
- Symptoms:
  - First request p95 > 2s; subsequent steady-state requests within SLO.
- Immediate mitigation:
  - Use short-lived warmup traffic after deploy via internal warmup job: ./scripts/warmup.sh --model $MODEL.
- Short-term remediation:
  - Preload commonly used model variants into warm pools.
- Long-term remediation:
  - Optimize binary load path and introduce a lightweight shadow-warm-start path that avoids heavy memory copies.
- Owner: runtime-startup team.

9) Telemetry sampling gap / delayed traces
- Symptoms:
  - Lost traces with sampling rate drop; alerts missing for a class of errors.
  - Traces show large gaps in walltime or missing service spans.
- Immediate mitigation:
  - Re-enable fallback tracer and increase sampling rate to 100% for the affected service: OTEL_SAMPLER_PROBABILITY=1.0.
- Short-term remediation:
  - Fix the collector pipeline and replay buffered telemetry.
- Long-term remediation:
  - Harden exporter backpressure handling and add local persisted buffer for telemetry.
- Owner: observability team.

On-call quick playbook (ordered checklist):
1) Identify & classify: use grafana + traces to map symptoms to one of the catalog rows.
2) Contain: if host-level, drain or detach the host. If network-level, adjust proxy timeouts.
3) Mitigate: apply runtime feature flags or routing overrides that are documented in the failure row.
4) Notify: inform product owner and customer success for impacted tenants when SLOs look threatened.
5) Record: open incident ticket and tag with the catalog failure ID.
6) Run post-incident action: add test coverage or automation as listed in long-term remediation.

Example detection rules (Prometheus + alert templates):
- Kernel latency alert (high):
  - name: HighKernelLatency
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_kernel_latency_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le, kernel, node)) > 2
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: "p99 kernel latency > 2s ({{ $labels.kernel }} on {{ $labels.node }})"

- GPU memory pressure alert:
  - name: GPUFreeBelow10pct
    expr: avg_over_time(node_gpu_memory_free_bytes[1m]) / node_gpu_memory_total_bytes < 0.10
    for: 1m
    labels:
      severity: page

Operational tooling & commands (handy snippets):
- Drain runtime host (orchestrator API):
  curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"$ORCH/api/v1/nodes/<node>/drain\"

- Validate kvcache shard (internal):
  curl -s -X POST \"$INTERNAL/kvcache/validate?shard=<id>\" | jq

- Temporary routing override (example):
  curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"model": "gpt-large", "route": "fallback-quantized", "duration_s": 600}' \"$PLATFORM/internal/routing/override\"

Metrics and dashboards to check (recommended panels):
- kernel latency by kernel and node (p50/p95/p99)
- node GPU memory free pct over time
- kvcache checksum errors by shard
- connection lifetime distribution for gRPC clients
- scheduler queue depth by priority class

Runbook maintenance and ownership:
- Each failure mode row must be reviewed quarterly by the owning team.
- When a remediation is completed, add a follow-up line with JIRA id and date in the row and remove the H/M flag if priority changes.
- Owners are responsible for adding unit/integration tests to CI that exercise the short-term mitigations.

Priority actions for next quarter (engineering backlog recommendations):
- Kernel team: implement handshake protocol and ship kernel-level test harness (JIRA: RUNTIME-8421).
- Memory/allocator squad: implement preflight dynamic accounting (JIRA: MEMACC-330).
- Scheduler team: land preemptive slice rollout with integration test (JIRA: SCHED-214).
- Observability: add persisted telemetry buffer and 100% sampling toggle for incident windows (JIRA: OBS-120).

Appendices:
A) Example incident ticket template (copy into new ticket):
- Title: [INCIDENT] <short summary of failure mode>
- Affected services: runtime, scheduler
- Impact: routes, tenants, SLOs impacted
- Detection: Grafana panel + trace link
- Immediate mitigations applied: list commands and flags
- Owner: <owner-team>
- Next steps: short-term fix, long-term fix, test needed

B) Glossary of internal endpoints used in this doc:
- $ORCH: internal orchestrator API (https://orch.internal)
- $PLATFORM: platform control API (https://platform.internal)
- $INTERNAL: runtime internal admin API (https://runtime-admin.internal)

C) Change log:
- 2025-10-14: created — initial catalog of 7 failure modes (S. Martinez)
- 2025-12-02: added NVLink and telemetry gaps; clarified on-call steps (reviewers: A. Patel, L. Nguyen)
- 2026-02-09: updated mitigation commands and added short-term remediation for model-swap oscillation (M. Chen)

If you are on-call and this page does not match the incident you see, escalate to the runtime escalation channel (#runtime-ops) and update this page with the observed new signals so we can keep the inventory current.
